questions.q: What method does the lesson teach for answering most AI engineering interview questions?
options: Memorize one confident, fixed answer to recite for every version of the question
Name the real tradeoff, state your default, and name the condition that would change it
Avoid giving any specific answer and change the subject
Always answer with the longest possible list of buzzwords
questions.explain: The lesson's core method is naming the tradeoff, giving a default answer, and naming what condition would change that answer -- a stronger signal than a memorized one-liner.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what should a RAG system do when retrieved context is only weakly related to the question?
options: Recognize the low relevance and say so, or ask a clarifying question, instead of forcing a confident guess
Always generate the most confident-sounding answer possible regardless of context quality
Discard the question entirely and never respond
Automatically switch to a completely unrelated document set
questions.explain: The lesson identifies forcing an answer from weak context as a primary hallucination source, and recommends honestly flagging low relevance instead.

questions.q: What makes a prompting decision defensible in an interview, according to the lesson?
options: Saying the structure simply 'felt right' with no further explanation
Choosing the longest possible prompt regardless of outcome
That it was changed because of an observed failure, with a clear before/after
Copying a prompt structure from an unrelated project without adaptation
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly warns against 'it felt right' and instead defines a defensible decision as one tied to an observed failure and its fix.

questions.q: What does the lesson say actually stops an agent from doing something destructive?
options: A single powerful safety rule that makes every other safeguard unnecessary
Relying entirely on the model's own judgment with no external checks
Several layered defenses together: scoped tools, human approval, action limits, and audit logging
Giving the agent as many broad, general-purpose tools as possible
questions.explain: The lesson frames agent safety as a layered-defense question, where naming multiple independent safeguards signals production thinking, not a single fix.

questions.q: When asked how to speed up a slow RAG system, what does the lesson say to do first?
options: Immediately switch to the cheapest available model with no measurement
Measure where time actually goes across each stage -- embedding, search, re-ranking, generation -- before optimizing
Assume the generation call is always the slowest stage without checking
Remove the evaluation pipeline to save processing time
questions.explain: The lesson recommends measuring each pipeline stage separately rather than guessing which one to optimize first.
